definition: A condition occurring when an internal organ or tissue pushes through a weakness or preexisting opening in surrounding muscle or connective tissue.
general_symptoms: Visible lump or bulge that appears during certain activities or in certain physical positions and goes back in at other times
Pinching when the hernia comes out
Sharp pain when the hernia comes through the opening
general_causes: Gradual occurrence as you get older and regular wear and tear on your muscles begins to add up
Weakness or a preexisting opening in your muscle or connective tissue
general_diagnosis_methods: Asking you to cough or adjust your position
Soft tissue imaging, such as a CT scan
general_treatments: Surgical repair (pushing herniated tissue back into place and reinforcing the barrier with stitches or surgical mesh)
Minimally-invasive methods (laparoscopic surgery or robotic surgery)
general_outlook: Most aren’t serious, but they can be and can become more serious over time
Tend to worsen over time, most will need surgical repair sooner or later
Small hernia may never bother you much, but hernias tend to grow bigger over time
Surgery is usually a simple outpatient procedure with a short recovery
Surgery is almost always successful, but there is a 10% chance of the hernia returning sometime later
complications: Incarceration (hernia getting stuck in the hole and unable to go back in)
Strangulation (tissue cut off from blood supply)
Surgical complications: excessive bleeding, wound infection, reactions to anesthesia, short-term difficulty urinating
living_with: Adjust habits or the nature of work to avoid straining the hernia
Wearing a special restraining belt to hold it in during certain activities
Pay attention to symptoms and any changes experienced

causes: Part of your bowel protruding into your inguinal canal
specific_symptoms: Visible scrotal swelling in people with testicles
complications: Chronic groin pain after inguinal hernia repair

Causing babies to be critically ill

Part of your intestine poking through an opening in your abdominal wall near your belly button
